claims.text: Standard high-energy laser melting of AlCrFeNiSi creates steep thermal gradients.
Standard high-energy laser melting of AlCrFeNiSi produces high residual stresses.
Standard high-energy laser melting of AlCrFeNiSi produces heterogeneous microstructures and degraded mechanical performance.
A low-energy laser pass immediately after each deposited layer can produce controlled partial remelting and in-situ annealing of that layer.
Reduced laser power, slower scan speed, and increased dwell time will deliver a lower energy density than the primary melting step.
The proposed process is applicable to miniature components with complex geometries under room-temperature build conditions.
Enhanced atomic diffusion during the secondary thermal cycle promotes residual-stress relaxation.
Enhanced atomic diffusion during the secondary thermal cycle promotes grain refinement and reduces microstructural inhomogeneity.
The secondary thermal cycle improves bonding between deposited layers.
The secondary pass can heat solidified material enough for partial remelting without destroying the previously formed geometry.
Controlled secondary thermal exposure relieves residual stress through recovery processes.
Controlled secondary thermal exposure produces a more uniform grain structure with less segregation.
Components receiving the secondary pass will have lower residual stress than components made with only a conventional high-energy pass.
Components receiving the secondary pass will contain fewer processing-induced defects.
Components receiving the secondary pass will have a better balance of yield strength and ductility.
Excess secondary energy input can cause grain growth, deleterious phase changes or oxidation and thereby worsen microstructural integrity.
The optimal laser energy, scan parameters, and phase-stable processing window have not been determined.
Failure to obtain statistically significant reductions in residual stress together with improvements in microstructural uniformity and mechanical properties would falsify the hypothesis.

contradictions.description: The intervention is defined as low-energy, but slower scan speed and longer dwell generally increase local energy input for a given power. Without quantitative power, speed, spot-size, and dwell values, the stated parameter directions do not necessarily produce the claimed lower energy density.
